title: The finite-cutoff nonlinear ground energy has quartic scale

ground_energy.bootstrap_assumption: Suppose q0[psi]+gE_nu W_N<=epsilon N^4 for a normalized cutoff state and fixed g>0
ground_energy.quantitative_shell_covariance: K1539 supplies c0>0 such that choosing epsilon<c0 forces T_N>C_sh,N/2>=kappa C_N/2; this uses its explicit low-shell Fisher floor rather than an o(N^4) limit
ground_energy.amplitude_error: K1538 gives r_N=E_nu|||phi_N|-sqrt(3C_N)||_2^2<=E_nu W_N/(3C_N), hence r_N/C_N<=epsilon/(3g c_C^2) when C_N>=c_C N^2
ground_energy.sign_shell_release: K1541's projection factorization yields E_nu H_N>=T_N/(6C_N)-r_N/(3C_N)>=kappa/12-epsilon/(9g c_C^2); for epsilon small this is at least kappa/24
ground_energy.interaction_contradiction: K1556 then gives E_nu W_N>=c1 N^4; choosing epsilon<g c1 contradicts the bootstrap assumption
ground_energy.lower_and_upper: Thus E_N>=c_g N^4 for all large N, while the vacuum has q0=0 and E W_N=6C_N^2=O(N^4), so E_N=Theta_g(N^4)
ground_energy.resolvent_consequence: For fixed lambda>=0, ||(H_N+lambda)^(-1)||=O_g(N^-4), and every scalar recentering a_N=o(N^4) remains coercively divergent
ground_energy.scope_guard: Theta_g(N^4) identifies only the cutoff exponent up to coupling-dependent constants; it does not determine E_N to O(1), a ground-state profile, compactness, Mosco recovery, a continuum interacting BRST operator or a source-owned GU Hamiltonian
